correctness.rationale: For m>=2 and a>0, the standard complex Gaussian logarithmic potential gives expected planar density (4pi)^(-1)Delta log(1+a*r^(2m)+r^(4m)). Independent differentiation yields exactly rho=2m²/(pi*r²)*(a cosh x+2)/(a+2cosh x)^2 with x=2m log r, including rho->0 at r->0/infinity and expected total degree 2m. Derivative in x of log rho equals h_a(x)-1/m; independently verified its rational hyperbolic derivative identity. The sign of h_a prime reduces to one affine comparison in cosh x, allowing at most one local maximum on x>0. For a>4 its positive hump has height H(a)=2(t²-1)^(3/2)/sqrt(4t^6-1), t=(a/4)^(1/3), increasing strictly from 0 to 1; equality to 1/m has exactly one u=t²>1 solving 4m²(u-1)^3=4u^3-1. Below/on/above threshold there are zero/one tangency/two positive-x derivative roots; the unique negative-x maximum persists, so the one-to-two strict radial maxima classification holds. The tangency is cubic shoulder not peak; nondegenerate fold follows from second and parameter derivatives. The asymptotic m^(-2/3) follows from the defining cubic. Numerical root checks are supportive only; the sign derivation handles the full real radius domain.
residual_risks: The classification is for expected *planar area* density, not radial count Jacobian or realizations.
The script finite sample does not establish the all-m theorem; analytic monotonicity does.
